question: What happens to the inter-particle space when a solid melts into a liquid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a **solid melts into a liquid**, its particles gain energy and move more freely. This results in an **increase in inter-particle space**, as the rigid structure of the solid is broken.
 
• In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a fixed, rigid lattice structure. This arrangement has **minimal inter-particle space**, making solids incompressible and dense.
 
• When heat is applied to a solid, its particles absorb energy. This energy increases the **vibrational motion** of the particles, weakening the intermolecular forces that hold them together in a fixed position.
 
• As the intermolecular forces weaken, the particles begin to move more freely, transitioning the material from a solid to a liquid state. This increased movement causes the **inter-particle space to expand**.
 
• The **melting point** of a substance is the temperature at which this transition occurs, and it is a physical property unique to each substance.
